terra.problem: “Wrong stop” uses “wrong” about the baker’s answer.
“No arguing, no stalling” asserts details the text does not give. “A different man walks back” also risks contradicting the passage’s emphasis that he is the same man.
Jesus tells the man to wash, but the text does not say He predicted the result to him.
The joke refers to a twin theory, but neither the passage nor the answer proposes a twin. The comparison does not follow from the card.
“A man will always be honest” makes an unsupported claim about how this man will behave.
The passage does not say the Sabbath was not also a fasting day. It simply does not mention fasting.
“He doesn’t hold anything back” goes beyond the text. His answer here does not include every detail of the healing.
The text reports a division among the Pharisees, but does not say this one question caused it.
“He’s thinking it through” states his unrecorded thought process as fact.
Being born blind does not mean his eyes were closed all his life. The text does not say that.
“Close in sound” does not make sense as a comparison between “deaf” and “blind.”
The man going to the pool does not establish that he could “walk fine.”
The explanation assigns their willingness to speak to their certainty. The passage gives their fear of the Jews as the reason for their answer.
The passage says what the Jews had determined, but does not say the parents had heard about that decision.
The explanation states a fact about the synagogue beyond this passage without a supporting reference.
Arguing with a mixing bowl does not match the man’s bold response to repeated questioning. The joke’s comparison does not connect.
Calling Moses Israel’s leader is a Bible fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The descriptions of Abraham as Israel’s forefather and Moses as Israel’s leader are facts from outside this passage and need references.
The descriptions of Elijah as a prophet of Israel and Moses as Israel’s leader are facts from outside this passage and need references.
“This had no track record” turns the man’s statement about what anyone had heard into an unqualified historical claim.
Calling Egypt a nation from Israel’s history introduces a Bible fact from outside the passage without a reference.
Calling Babylon a nation from Israel’s history introduces a Bible fact from outside the passage without a reference.
The passage does not say the Jews did not go looking for Jesus. It says they threw the man out and Jesus found him.
“He’s already had his eyes opened, so” assigns a reason for his question that the text does not give.
The text does not say he was begging by a road, that all these events happened on the same day, or that he knelt to worship.
“No hesitation” adds a detail about the timing of his response that the text does not give.
Saying the statement “landed on them” and “hits close to home” assigns an unmarked reaction and reason for their question.
Calling the earlier statement a “worry” assigns a feeling the text does not state.
The passage records Jesus saying they claim to see; it does not record them saying they could see.
